title: 建築環境設計Ⅰ
subtitle: Environmental Design for Architecture I
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) learn about current conditions and methods for realizing zero-energy buildings.
(2) learn about current conditions and methods for realizing green buildings.
(3) learn about calculation of heat load and cooling coil capability.
advice: As an advanced stage of learning about architectural thermal environment and air conditioning, students will learn about actual examples of human body temperature cold sensation evaluation, methods for calculating residential heat loss coefficients, and on-site condensation checks. Furthermore, in order to realize energy-saving buildings, students will acquire the latest knowledge about national energy-saving standards, the concept of primary energy consumption, and ZEB. In order to learn about regional collaboration, students will investigate energy-saving buildings located in each region. In addition, students will learn the basics of air-conditioning equipment design by calculating the indoor load of a building and the capacity of the required cooling coil through exercises.
requiredKnowledge: Students need credits from Introduction of Building Equipment, Architectural Environment I and II, and Building Equipment.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain terms related to zero energy buildings.
Be able to explain terms related to environmental architecture.
The processes of heating, cooling, humidification, and dehumidification can be represented on a chart.
Be able to explain the latest equipment for next-generation architecture.
Building heat load calculations can be done manually.
It is possible to calculate the cooling coil capacity in an air conditioner.

achievementLevels.ideal: With regard to energy-saving architecture, various proposals can be made based on the location and various conditions of the building, while referring to thermal environment performance and primary energy consumption.
achievementLevels.standard: To be able to present methods for expressing thermal environment performance and energy saving methods for the realization of energy saving buildings.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              As an advanced stage of learning about architectural thermal environment and air conditioning, students will learn about actual examples of human body temperature cold sensation evaluation, methods for calculating residential heat loss coefficients, and on-site condensation checks. Furthermore, in order to realize energy-saving buildings, students will acquire the latest knowledge about national energy-saving standards, the concept of primary energy consumption, and ZEB. In order to learn about regional collaboration, students will investigate energy-saving buildings located in each region. In addition, students will learn the basics of air-conditioning equipment design by calculating the indoor load of a building and the capacity of the required cooling coil through exercises.
